subject: Lyra pilot: prefetch, batching & tokens-per-dollar probes
messages:
From: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@lyrahealth.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@lyrahealth.com
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot MAP — clarify tokens/$ assumptions for clinical triage POC

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile and the observability UI. As we align the MAP for the clinical triage pilot, our procurement and engineering leads have asked for a short write-up on the cost assumptions you used in the MAP draft: tokens per API call (avg), any prefetch/prefix caching you recommend, and batching guidance for our expected traffic (50–200 qps during business hours).

Can you confirm: 1) the tokens/(response+prompt) you modeled for a typical triage request, 2) whether Redwood suggests synchronous small-batch inference or aggressive micro-batching with a 10–30ms queue, and 3) what unit cost numbers you used (tokens/$) for the Hosted vs Dedicated pricing in the MAP? Procurement also asked for any sensitivity scenarios we should present to finance.

If easier, we can take a 30-min call with your pre-sales/finops folks — we aim to finalize MAP milestones and cost gates by Aug 25.

Appreciate it,
Sarah
Sarah Patel
Head of Platform Integrations, Lyra Health
From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@lyrahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP — clarify tokens/$ assumptions for clinical triage POC

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. I attached a short MAP appendix (lyra_map_draft_v1.pdf) and a sample traffic CSV with our baseline sampler. High-level answers here and a suggested agenda if we schedule the 30-min call: 

Quick answers (TL;DR):
- Modeled avg tokens per triage request: 420 tokens (60 prompt + 360 response).
- Prefetch/prefix caching: recommend prefix caching for patient context (saves ~18–28% tokens depending on prompt reuse).
- Batching: for your profile (50–200 qps) we recommend hybrid: synchronous single-request path for <60ms SLOs and micro-batch windowing (5–10ms) for ~10% of traffic that can tolerate slight added latency — reduces unit cost by ~12–16% in our sims.
- Unit numbers used in MAP: Hosted baseline: 1M tokens = $5.60 (effective tokens/$ = 178,571 tokens per $); Dedicated reserved: modeled at $3.10 / 1M tokens (322,580 tokens per $) after committed capacity and quantization savings.

Suggested 30-min call agenda: 1) confirm traffic shape & SLOs, 2) review MAP cost-sensitivity worksheet (I can screen-share the perf sims), 3) agree on gating thresholds for prefetched context, batching windows, and rollout stash.

If that works I can loop in Mina (solutions) and Karthik (infra) for the call. Available Thu 8/19 10:00–11:00 PT or 8/19 14:00–15:00 PT.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: mina.haddad@redwood.ai <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pilot MAP — clarify tokens/$ assumptions for clinical triage POC

Kimberly — quick internal note before we jump on the call. Key things to validate in the MAP appendix so Lyra procurement can sign off: 
- Break out tokens per component: prompt template (patient+instructions), model system prompt, and average response. We should show 3 scenarios (p50/p75/p95 tokens).
- Prefetch assumptions: show a conservative and optimistic reuse rate; conservative (10% reuse) yields ~6% savings, optimistic (35% reuse) yields ~22% savings — explicitly call out stateful vs stateless caching tradeoffs for PHI contexts.
- Batching: include micro-batch trade table with latency delta at 5ms/10ms/20ms windows and corresponding cost reduction percentages. Put numerical examples for 100 qps and 200 qps.
- Quantization/instance sizing: include the quantization tier we used to get the Dedicated numbers (4-bit hybrid) and the expected throughput per GPU. Procurement often flags unsupported quantization claims so be explicit.

Also: recommend we attach a short sensitivity CSV (I put a sample_traffic_profile.csv) that finance can run locally. I'll prep the p50/p75/p95 numbers and a onepager for SRE considerations.

-Mina
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: mina.haddad@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 09:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP — clarify tokens/$ assumptions for clinical triage POC

Adding infra notes in-line: 
- GPUs & quantization: Dedicated $3.10 / 1M token assumes TFLOP/memory characteristics for our 4-bit optimized runtime on NVIDIA H100x2 equivalent. We should call out fallback to fp16 when customer demands full-fidelity outputs (adjusted unit price +18%).
- Batching windows: micro-batches of 5–10ms are realistic if the front-end accepts a 10–20ms P99 tail increase for that subset of traffic. For Lyra's target 60ms SLO, we should cap micro-batch exposure at 15% traffic.
- Prefetch security: when caching PHI we need to signal Lyra's compliance team we will keep prefetch TTLs short and ensure KMS-bound key usage for any persisted contexts. Mention that Private deployment can avoid prefix leaving their VPC.
- Throughput sims: for 100qps with 10% micro-batching and 25% prefix reuse we project 14% cost reduction vs no-caching/no-batching. Attach the sim spreadsheet on the call.

-Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@lyrahealth.com>, procurement@lyrahealth.com
Cc: mina.haddad@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP — clarify tokens/$ assumptions for clinical triage POC

Sarah — thanks, we pulled the MAP appendix together and annotated the sensitivity scenarios you asked for (see attached lyra_map_draft_v1.pdf and sample_traffic_profile.csv). Summary highlights for procurement and finance: 

1) Baseline token model: p50=310 tokens, p75=420 tokens, p95=760 tokens per request (includes system prompt and avg response). We used p75=420 as the MAP default.
2) Unit economics: Hosted: $5.60 per 1M tokens (map baseline). Dedicated modeled after 12-month commit + 4-bit quantization: $3.10 per 1M tokens. Note: fallback to fp16 (customer-requested fidelity) raises effective Hosted/Dedicated cost by ~18%.
3) Caching: conservative reuse (10%) = ~6% cost saving; optimistic reuse (30%) = ~20% cost saving. We call out compliance controls for caching PHI (TTL, KMS, VPC-only option).
4) Batching policy recommended: default sync path for 85% traffic (SLO-sensitive), micro-batch 5–10ms for up to 15% non-SLO traffic. Projected combined savings at 100qps = ~12–15%.

Action items / next steps: 
- Sarah/Procurement: confirm whether Lyra prefers Hosted POC or a short Dedicated pilot to validate the committed ratecard (we recommended Dedicated for predictability if Lyra expects sustained >10M tokens/mo).
- Finance: run sensitivity CSV (attached) for p50/p75/p95 to validate budget thresholds.
- Redwood: schedule 30-min call to walk through sims — proposed Thu 8/19 14:00–14:30 PT.

If you confirm the call I'll send a calendar invite and include the sim workbook.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
